note: Curated New England solar / net-metering / REC market / regulatory updates for array operators. Each item is tagged with its state (or "region" for New England-wide, "rec" for REC-market-wide); the page filters to the reader's state. Refreshed by a research agent; verify against the linked source before relying on any figure.

items.title: ISO New England logs its 500th 'duck curve' day as behind-the-meter solar keeps climbing
items.summary: ISO New England said the grid hit its 500th 'duck curve' day on September 21, 2026 — the 107th of 2026 alone — as rooftop and other behind-the-meter solar drive midday grid demand below overnight levels. Behind-the-meter PV set a record estimated output of about 7,068 MW around 1 p.m. on April 8, 2026, and the ISO estimates these resources generated 9,926 GWh in 2025.

items.title: Massachusetts energy-affordability bill stays stalled in conference as Healey weighs winter relief
items.summary: As of late September 2026 the Massachusetts omnibus energy-affordability bill remained in a House-Senate conference committee with no deal, prompting Gov. Maura Healey to say her administration is weighing direct relief for households heading into winter. The pending legislation would leave residential rooftop net metering intact while trimming net-metering credit values for larger non-residential facilities.

items.title: Connecticut standard-service rates keep falling as public-benefits bill credit runs through April 2027
items.summary: A Sept 17, 2026 CT Mirror report notes electricity prices are falling heading into the election: Eversource standard-service supply dropped to 11.577¢/kWh on July 1, 2026 and a public-benefits bill credit of roughly $30–34/month runs through April 2027, driven largely by long-term Millstone and Seabrook nuclear contracts. Eversource's pending PURA distribution rate case still seeks a double-digit increase for July 2027.

items.title: Power Advisory: New England basic service rates jump ~14% for 2H 2026, lifting net-metering payouts
items.summary: A Sept 14, 2026 Power Advisory report finds second-half 2026 basic/standard-service supply rates rose about 14% on average across six New England utilities year-over-year — roughly 14% in Massachusetts, 15% in Rhode Island, 25% in New Hampshire and 3% in Connecticut — driven by elevated gas prices, a harsh winter and NECEC underperformance. Because net-metering and community-solar compensation is linked to basic service rates, the analysis notes project owners will see higher payouts, with a further ~12% average increase projected for 1H 2027 (Eversource CT up ~25%).

items.title: Vermont PUC opens a rulemaking to update net-metering Rule 5.100, with an Oct 2 workshop
items.summary: On September 9, 2026 the Vermont Public Utility Commission issued an order opening an investigation to update Commission Rule 5.100 (Regulations Pertaining to Construction and Operation of Net-Metering Systems). A stakeholder workshop is scheduled for October 2, 2026 at 9:30 a.m. The rulemaking follows the Commission's May 29, 2026 biennial compensation update that cut Category I rates for a seventh straight year.

items.title: Vermont PUC finalizes a 5.5% Green Mountain Power rate increase (Case 26-0096-TF), below the 7.5% requested
items.summary: The Vermont Public Utility Commission's Aug 28, 2026 order approved a 5.5% distribution rate increase for Green Mountain Power's 275,000+ customers — below the 7.5% the utility sought (Case 26-0096-TF) — effective Oct 1, 2026. Regulators approved about $113 million of 'resilience' infrastructure spending, roughly a third of GMP's $341 million request, citing affordability as central to the analysis.

items.title: Maine DOER proposes a Front-of-the-Meter DER program for renewables cut out of Net Energy Billing
items.summary: Maine's Department of Energy Resources published a draft Front-of-the-Meter Distributed Energy Resources (FTM DER) program proposal in late August 2026 — a successor pathway for larger renewable projects excluded from Net Energy Billing under LD 1777. DOER held a Sept 2 webinar, took written comments through Sept 11, and must submit a program design to the MPUC by Sept 30, 2026; the program would let projects contract with utilities and feed the standard offer.

items.title: Gov. Healey signs data-center executive order shielding ratepayers as omnibus energy bill stays in conference
items.summary: Governor Maura Healey signed an executive order on Sept 8, 2026 requiring new data centers to meet their power demand with clean energy, obtain local approval, and cover their own grid costs to protect ratepayers. Advocates urged it as a model for the stalled energy-affordability bill (S.3143 / H.5175), which remained in conference committee; that bill would leave residential rooftop net metering intact while trimming credits for large non-residential facilities.

items.title: Rhode Island Energy's new base distribution rates take effect September 1 (Docket 25-45-GE compliance)
items.summary: Rhode Island Energy made its compliance filing on August 27, 2026 and the RI PUC-approved base distribution increase took effect September 1, 2026. A typical residential electric bill rises about $7.78/month (≈4.83%) in the first year, while roughly $170 million in accelerated bill credits flow to customers from October 2026 through September 2027 under a hold-harmless structure.

items.title: Rhode Island Energy files net-metering overhaul in Docket 26-30-EL cutting the remote cap to 175 MW
items.summary: On August 14, 2026 Rhode Island Energy filed a revised net-metering provision (Docket 26-30-EL, proposed effective Sept 13, 2026) that lowers the aggregate ground-mount remote-net-metering cap from 275 MW to 175 MW, extends the qualifying-project deadline from July 1, 2030 to Dec 31, 2032, and adds an optional 25-year 'Fixed Renewable Net Metering Credit' of 19¢/kWh (escalating 2.75%/yr from 2028) for public, educational, hospital and nonprofit systems. The filing is pending before the PUC.

items.title: Power Advisory: New England Class I RECs hold near the $40 ACP into a sixth undersupplied year
items.summary: An August 2026 Power Advisory update reports New England Class I RECs have traded close to the $40 Alternative Compliance Payment through a sixth straight undersupplied year, with forwards (Marex Spectron, as of Aug 13, 2026) still near the cap. Rhode Island has aligned its RES ACP to $40 flat, making the ceiling uniform across MA, CT and RI; separately, NECEC Quebec hydro (delivering since January 2026) is expected to cover nearly all of the Massachusetts Clean Energy Standard requirement in CY2026.

items.title: Rhode Island aligns its RES Alternative Compliance Payment to $40 flat, adding regional Class I supply
items.summary: Rhode Island's FY2027 budget (enacted June 2026) lowered the state's Renewable Energy Standard Alternative Compliance Payment to $40/MWh flat nominal — down from roughly $87 and no longer indexed to CPI — bringing it in line with Massachusetts and Connecticut, per an Aug 17, 2026 Power Advisory analysis. The change, together with broadened existing-renewable eligibility, effectively increases regional Class I REC supply.

items.title: Acadia Center granted intervenor status in Eversource's Connecticut distribution rate case
items.summary: On August 14, 2026 Acadia Center was granted intervenor status in Eversource's pending PURA rate case, where the utility seeks up to an 18% bill increase. Acadia is challenging the requested 10.25% return on equity as 'unreasonable and out of step with ROEs nationwide' and is pushing for performance-based ratemaking.

items.title: Rhode Island Energy asks PUC to raise winter Last Resort Service to 17.029¢/kWh (Docket 26-27-EL)
items.summary: On July 22–24, 2026 Rhode Island Energy filed to raise its residential Last Resort Service supply rate to 17.029¢/kWh for the Oct 1, 2026–Mar 31, 2027 winter period — about 15% above last winter's 14.77¢/kWh, roughly $12/month more for a typical 500 kWh home. The rate remained subject to final PUC approval as of mid-September 2026, with the interim page still showing 11.092¢/kWh through September.

items.title: Maine DOER files first competitive energy-storage solicitation seeking up to 360 MW
items.summary: Maine's Department of Energy Resources filed its first competitive energy-storage solicitation on July 20, 2026, seeking up to 360 MW toward the state's statutory 400 MW-by-2030 storage goal. The MPUC has up to 120 days to review the filing for statutory compliance before a formal RFP issues, with project selections expected by the end of 2026.

items.title: Broker quotes put MA Class I RECs at $38–$42/MWh as Gridwealth adds REC-supply products
items.summary: Gridwealth Electric launched six new C&I supply structures for New England, including a 100% MA Class I REC bundle aimed at Boston BERDO compliance, stating MA Class I certificates 'currently trade around $38 to $42' per MWh. Competitive Energy Services corroborates the market 'trading just below $40,' with 2025 compliance met partly via Alternative Compliance Payments.

items.title: NH Gov. Ayotte signs SB 538 extending net metering for queued municipal solar
items.summary: SB 538 (Chapter 315, effective Sept 8, 2026) supports municipal solar projects up to 5 MW and guarantees the current net-metering credit for 20 years for cities, towns, school districts and counties whose projects were already in the interconnection queue. It was signed July 10, 2026.

items.title: SMART 3.0 applications flow but Final Qualifications await DPU tariff approval (Docket 25-175)
items.summary: As of mid-September 2026, DOER continues accepting SMART 3.0 applications and issuing Preliminary Statements of Qualification but will not issue Final Statements — or start incentive payments — until the model tariff clears DPU Docket 25-175. The DPU approved the model tariffs without modification on May 19, 2026 but deferred outstanding issues to a Phase II; the 20-year SMART term begins only after tariff approval and a project's Final Statement of Qualification.
